Corporate.vision: There's an opening for a mid-size firm that wins on operational discipline and modern reporting.

Corporate.tagline: Integrated marketing and brand services for mid-market companies.
Corporate.brandNameRationale: Selwyn is a surname with a senior, slightly establishment register. Creative Group signals the agency category with a structural word — group implies multiple disciplines under one roof. Together it reads as a serious integrated agency, not a boutique.
Corporate.manifesto: Selwyn Creative Group is a multi-discipline marketing agency for mid-market companies — brand, creative, digital, media, PR — under one roster. The buyer is a CMO with a quarterly board to report to. The engagement is the year, not the project. The work is the campaign and the metric.
Corporate.industrySummary: Mid-market companies are increasingly under-served by holding-company agencies (too expensive, too slow) and by boutiques (too narrow). The opening is for a serious integrated agency that can stand up brand, creative, digital, and media under a single account team.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: Mother (motherlondon.com) is the closest creative-led peer at scale. R/GA (rga.com) defines the integrated holding-company offering. Joan Creative (joancreative.com) holds the boutique-integrated middle. We sit between the boutique and the holding-company offerings, mid-market focused.
Corporate.positioningStatement: Selwyn Creative Group is a mid-market integrated marketing agency operating brand, creative, digital, media, and PR under one account team.
Corporate.positioningRationale: We compete on integration and senior-team continuity. One account director, one project lead, one creative lead — across all five disciplines, for the year.

targetAudience.primary: CMOs and VPs of marketing at companies with $50M–$500M in revenue, running annual marketing programs.
behaviors: Manage three to seven agency relationships at once.

Want one calendar across brand, creative, digital, media, PR.

dos: Lead with the marketing problem, then the work.

Reference real metric improvements in case studies.

Corporate.brandDescription: Hartcourt Creative Holdings operates a portfolio of creative agency brands across brand strategy, advertising, digital production, and content creation categories.
Corporate.scope:
Hartcourt Creative Holdings works across:
• Multi-brand creative agency operations
• Shared new-business development across the portfolio
• Cross-agency talent and resource sharing
• Client-relationship coordination across brands
• Annual investor and operator reporting
Corporate.mission: To provide a serious operating platform for mid-tier creative agency brands that want to keep their identity and outsource the operations.
Corporate.vision: A creative agency operator whose portfolio brands grow under their own names because the new-business and operations are shared.
coreValues: Senior — partners deal with partners.
Operational — new-business and operations run on schedule.
Reliable — predictable operations across agencies.
Discreet — agency relationships stay private.
Corporate.brandNameRationale: Hartcourt is a real English surname with a heritage trade register. Creative Holdings follows the multi-brand operator naming convention used in advertising (WPP, Omnicom Group, Interpublic Group, Publicis Groupe structure). The pair reads as an institutional operator with multi-brand portfolio scale.
Corporate.manifesto: Hartcourt Creative Holdings owns and operates a portfolio of creative agency brands. Each brand retains its identity, creative direction, and client relationships; we operate the shared new-business development, finance, and back office. The buyer is an agency founder considering sale, a holding company seeking single-vendor agency relationships, or an institutional investor holding creative-agency assets.
Corporate.industrySummary: Creative agencies have consolidated under a small number of large multi-brand holding companies (WPP, Omnicom, Interpublic, Publicis). The opening underneath is for a regional mid-tier multi-brand operator with deep new-business operations and the procurement-grade reliability holding-company partners require.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: WPP (wpp.com) is the multi-brand agency reference. Omnicom Group (omnicomgroup.com) holds the multi-brand peer slot. Interpublic Group (interpublic.com) sits in the multi-brand peer position. Stagwell Inc (stagwellglobal.com) plays the modern multi-brand peer reference. We belong in the regional mid-tier multi-brand creative-agency operator category.
Corporate.positioningStatement: Hartcourt Creative Holdings is a regional multi-brand creative agency operator running new-business, talent, and shared operations across a portfolio of agency brands.
Corporate.positioningRationale: We compete on shared new-business depth, cross-agency talent, and the operational reliability agency founders need without giving up creative direction.

targetAudience.primary: Agency founders considering sale, holding companies seeking single-vendor agency relationships, and institutional investors holding creative-agency assets.
behaviors: Manage multi-brand agency operations.
Negotiate multi-year client and talent agreements.
Care about new-business pipeline, creative retention, and client renewal rates.
Renew on multi-year operating terms.
motivations: Need an operator with shared new-business operations.
Need to keep brand identity and creative direction post-acquisition.
Need a single-vendor multi-brand agency relationship.

dos: Lead with brand portfolio, client roster, and creative-team retention.
Speak the language of agency founders, holding-company executives, and procurement.
Publish quarterly operator letters.
Refer to agencies by name, not by Hartcourt tagging.
donts: No social media at the parent level.
No brand consolidation announcements without partner alignment.

messagingPillars.name: Cross-agency talent
messagingPillars.description: Talent and resource sharing across the portfolio. Senior practitioners can engage across agencies as needed.

Corporate.logoDirection: A serif wordmark — Hartcourt set in a traditional book serif, with 'Creative Holdings' beneath in tracked small caps. Used in contracts and the corporate office. Not used on consumer-facing agencies.

typography.secondary: A clean enterprise grotesque for operational reports and agency documentation.

Creative.tagline: A studio that prints its work before sending it.
Creative.brandNameRationale: The Printed Office is a declarative title with the definite article — the convention of small named firms (The Innocence Project, The Public Domain Review). Stands in the lineage of declarative creative studios (Office for Bad Buildings, Office KGDVS).
Creative.manifesto: Most creative studios sand the edges off their work to make the client comfortable. We made Hard Copy because the work that lasts is the work that landed first and stayed. We sell the original idea, the one before the focus group, the one the client almost killed. We are not a safe agency. We are not for every client. We are for the ones who can recognize the hard copy.
Creative.industrySummary: Creative agency brand has been cautious and clean. There's room for a studio that's loud, opinionated, sticker-friendly, and still produces work that holds up under criticism.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Mother Design (motherdesign.com) holds the personality-forward studio position. Athletics (athletics.com) does the design-led-with-attitude middle. Order (order.design) sits closer in tone. We are sharper than all of them.
Creative.positioningStatement: A creative studio that pitches the original idea, not the safe one.

targetAudience.primary: 30 to 50. Founders, CMOs, and Creative Directors who are tired of holding-company work. They want a studio that will fight for the right answer, not the easy one.

dos: Show the original idea, not the one that shipped
Quote the brief and the rejection both
Make jokes about the agency industry
donts: Sand the edges off the work in case studies
Use the word strategic in a sentence with the word activation
Apologize for being a small studio

Creative.brandDescription: A creative studio that pitches the original idea, not the safe one.

Creative.vision: We are for the ones who can recognize the hard copy.

Creative.tagline: An agency that publishes its calendar.
Creative.brandNameRationale: Slow Studio is a declarative position against the always-on agency model. Two-word brand names with a point of view follow the creative declarative school (Office for Bad Buildings, Slow Walks Outdoor Co.).
Creative.manifesto: Most studios pretend they will start your project on Monday. We started Studio Later because the truth is more interesting — the good work is the work the studio actually had time to do, and time is the constraint nobody talks about. Our calendar is our most important deliverable. We are honest about it.
Creative.industrySummary: Studios over-promise on timelines and under-deliver on attention. The market is full of clients who would prefer honesty about lead times. There is a real opening for a studio brand built around its own calendar.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Manual Creative (manualcreative.com) plays in the editorial-creative agency middle. Folk Studio (folkpattern.com) holds the warm-creative slot. Tundra Studio (tundra.studio) sits in the slow-craft peer position. We are louder and more upfront about the calendar than any of them.
Creative.positioningStatement: Studio Later is a creative studio that publishes its real availability and refuses to over-commit.
Creative.positioningRationale: The studio's calendar is the public artifact. New clients see, on the home page, what month we can start. The marketing is the schedule.

targetAudience.primary: Founders and marketing leaders who have been burned by studios that took on too much.
behaviors: Have hired a studio that disappeared mid-project.
Compare timelines in pitches.
Care about who is doing the work.
Wait for the studio they want.
motivations: Want a studio that is honest about timing.
Want to wait three months for the right team.
Want a public roadmap.

dos: Publish the calendar on the home page.
Tell clients early that the start date is later than they hoped.
Refer to the schedule by month.
Use the brand line — 'studio later' — in sign-offs.

Creative.tagline: A studio that publishes its working files.
Creative.brandDescription: The Open File Co is a creative-led design studio that publishes its working source files for every completed project as a primary deliverable, alongside the finished work.
Creative.scope:
The Open File Co works across:
• Design engagements with working files published alongside finished work
• Open-source design assets for past projects
• Educational programs for working designers based on the studio's process
• Quarterly published essays on design transparency
• Annual studio retrospective of published files
Creative.mission: To make design transparency a primary deliverable rather than an afterthought.
Creative.vision: A studio whose published working files become a standard reference for serious design practice.
coreValues: Specific — every working file is published.
Considered — transparency is a primary practice.
Warm — the design community benefits from the open files.
Literary — the writing about transparency is part of the brand.
Creative.brandNameRationale: The Open File is the universal designer's trade phrase for a working source file — and a phrase about transparency in creative work. The definite article + Co suffix follows the considered-creative trade-name school. The brand stakes a clear creative position around publishing source files as part of the work.
Creative.manifesto: Most design studios deliver the finished work and keep the working files private. We started The Open File Co to do the opposite — publish the working source files alongside the finished work as a primary deliverable. The transparency is the brand.
Creative.industrySummary: Design transparency is rare; most studios protect their process. There is real space for a creative-led brand that explicitly positions on published working files as primary deliverables.
Creative.competitorLandscape: MetaLab (metalab.com) holds the considered-modern studio peer slot. Build in Amsterdam (buildinamsterdam.com) plays the print-and-screen peer position. Order (order.design) sits in the minimal-modern peer position. Pentagram (pentagram.com) is the heritage peer reference. We sit further out — published working files as primary deliverable.
Creative.positioningStatement: The Open File Co is a design studio that publishes its working source files for every completed project as a primary deliverable.
Creative.positioningRationale: The brand competes on the transparency premise. Every project, every published file, and every essay is built around design transparency as a primary creative practice.

targetAudience.primary: Brand founders, design leads, and marketing teams commissioning design work who value transparency and process documentation.
behaviors: Want working files as part of the deliverable.
Care about design transparency and process documentation.
Plan to continue design work in-house after the engagement.
Want a studio that publishes its work.
motivations: Want published working files alongside finished work.
Want a studio with a transparency philosophy.
Want educational materials based on the studio's process.

dos: Publish the working files alongside finished projects.
Reference specific design decisions in case material.
Publish the quarterly essay on design transparency.
Sign correspondence by the principal designer.

messagingPillars.name: Published working files
messagingPillars.description: Every completed project ships with the working source files published alongside the finished work. The files are the deliverable.

messagingPillars.name: Open-source design assets
messagingPillars.description: Past project assets are published as open-source resources for the design community. The community uses them; the studio earns reputation.

messagingPillars.name: Quarterly essay
messagingPillars.description: The studio publishes a long-form essay on design transparency every quarter. The essay is the studio's primary marketing artefact.

Creative.logoDirection: A wordmark — The Open File Co set in a quiet display serif with a small illustration of a file-folder icon beside it. The mark appears in published source files and the studio's documentation.

colorPalette.meaning: Primary — the colour of a blank design file.

typography.rationale: The serif speaks. The grotesque files.
